result:
Round 426 is accepted and the round 427 task is ready. The decision is **CONTINUE**; nothing is blocked or complete.

**Round 426 (SYS-2 stage 2a, a held Enter acts once on the lane, group, master and tempo-row buttons):** C passed it with no bugs and real browser checks. I re-ran C's browser comparison on C's own results (ALL OK, 28 cells), and C's mutant summary matches mine exactly. Gate 426 published commit `052c76c`, which is the baseline for round 427. SYS-2 stage 2a is marked done.

**Round 427 (SYS-2 stage 2b-i):** I split the rest of stage 2b in two. This round covers the parts of the screen that stay open; the menus, dialogs and the shortcut sheet come next round.
- **The bug is real today.** In real Chromium, a held Enter keeps toggling these back and forth (14 of 18 test cells):
  - the Snap and Envelope buttons;
  - a library folder fold;
  - the detail panel;
  - the video float.

  After Close or Return docks the video, focus lands on Expand, so the held key floats it again.
- **What A applies:** a ready-made patch that adds the existing shared guard to 11 buttons in the library, detail panel, video dock and footer. It also moves 5 hand-written copies of the same guard onto that shared function. Nothing changes for a normal press, mouse click or Space, and nothing visible changes.
- **Tests:** a new test file with 9 rows. Each one turns red when its own guard is removed (12 mutants checked), and all 9 fail on today's code.
- **Already run on the patch:**
  - the 68 affected test files (1226 tests) and the full suite (266 files, 3984 tests) pass;
  - typecheck, lint and Biome are clean;
  - the browser comparison against today's code passes all 18 cells at 1440×900 and 1280×720, including where focus lands after each button;
  - mouse and Space behave exactly as before.
- **Review:** tech-lead approved with minor notes, and I folded its test fixes into the patch. A second tech-lead review of that change approved it.

**Corrections and rulings:**
- **TL-R425-09 (the Pan-reset-during-a-drag test that A's reviewer rated Medium):** the earlier reasoning was wrong. During a drag, the Studio refuses Enter before any button can click it, so that case can't be reached by keyboard. It is now pinned by a test that describes what actually happens.
- **A Low I filed and then withdrew:** I first recorded that the "can't edit while dragging" message is re-announced on every key repeat. Tech-lead's review and a stronger test show it is not, so it is closed as not a defect. A narrower variant (a repeat while the drag is also moving) stays as an unmeasured note.
- **Gate 426 architecture note:** it suggests replacing the per-button guard with a shared button or a lint check. I recorded it as a signal, not a task. A bounded frontend-architect checkpoint is planned for root once SYS-2 finishes.

**Next:**
- If round 427 passes, round 428 is SYS-2 stage 2b-ii, unless planning falls on or after 2026-11-13, when the regression round comes first.
- STEM-LANES still has no answer from Saba, and that doesn't block this work.
- One row stays BLOCKED for a reason outside A's work: the fake-token check against a real backend, because the backend isn't available in the cloud. It doesn't affect browser verification.

The advisor was available and consulted twice: after orientation and before closing. Its close check led to stronger focus checks in the browser comparison and to evidence for several claims about the current code that were previously unsupported. No store files were changed and nothing was committed.
